question.problem:
$$

Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{\operatorname{coth}⁡x}{{csch}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
$$

First, we find the hyperbolic identities that correspond to the following trigonometric identities:

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},\,\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identities are

$$
\operatorname{coth}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x},\,\operatorname{csch}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}.
$$

Now, we rewrite the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{\operatorname{coth}⁡x}{{csch}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\operatorname{coth}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{{csch}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}\cdot {sinh}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x.$ Then,

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $\frac{5}{3}$ |

Now, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{5/3}u\,\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}{|}_{1}^{5/3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({(\frac{5}{3})}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{25}{9}-1) \\  & =\frac{8}{9}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
